title: Trustpilot Reviews

companyDomains.title: Company domains
companyDomains.description: Companies by the domain Trustpilot lists them under — the part after trustpilot.com/review/ — e.g. ["www.booking.com", "n26.com", "ryanair.com"]; with or without www./https://; a website URL works too (scheme and path are stripped, then Trustpilot's own spelling is followed: monzo.com resolves to www.monzo.com). A bare company name does not: "Monzo" is rejected before anything is charged. Use for "reviews of company X": up to maxReviewsPerCompany reviews each at $0.0015 a review.
companyDomains.sectionDescription: Company domains and/or Trustpilot review-page URLs. At least one.

startUrls.title: Trustpilot review page URLs
startUrls.description: Trustpilot review-page URLs, e.g. ["https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.booking.com"]. Any query string on the URL is ignored — set the filters below instead; a country subdomain (uk.trustpilot.com, de.trustpilot.com) is read as the same profile. A URL and its bare domain in companyDomains count once, so mixing the two never double-bills. One of companyDomains or startUrls is required.

maxReviewsPerCompany.title: Max reviews per company
maxReviewsPerCompany.description: Reviews to return per company, 0 to 1000, e.g. 40 (default 100 = up to $0.15 per company). The main cost control. Trustpilot's filters and sinceDate apply BEFORE this cap, so 50 with maxRating 2 = the 50 newest 1- and 2-star reviews. 0 = every review Trustpilot serves without a login: 200 per filtered view, up to 1000 per company with deepPaging; the status row says capped: true when that wall, not the end of the reviews, stopped the walk.
maxReviewsPerCompany.sectionCaption: How many and in which order
maxReviewsPerCompany.sectionDescription: The cap is the main cost control; filters below apply before it.

sort.title: Order
sort.description: "most_recent" (default) = newest first, the order a monitoring schedule and sinceDate want. "most_relevant" = Trustpilot's own relevance order. Applied by Trustpilot.

minRating.title: Min rating (stars)
minRating.description: Lowest star rating to keep, 0 to 5, e.g. 4 for "positive reviews only" or "4 and 5 star reviews". 0 (default) = any rating. Combine with maxRating for a band. This is Trustpilot's own stars filter, applied on their servers: reviews outside it are never fetched or billed.
minRating.sectionDescription: Stars, date range, language, verified and keyword are Trustpilot's own filters and run on their side: rows they drop are never fetched, so never billed. sinceDate and requireText run in the actor, also before billing.

maxRating.title: Max rating (stars)
maxRating.description: Highest star rating to keep, 0 to 5, e.g. 2 for "negative reviews", "complaints", "1 and 2 star reviews". 0 (default) = any rating. Trustpilot's own stars filter, applied on their servers: on a 125,000-review brand maxRating 2 fetches and bills only the 1- and 2-star reviews. Add requireText true to drop rating-only rows.

sinceDate.title: Since date
sinceDate.description: Keep only reviews published on or after this date: "2026-09-01" (YYYY-MM-DD) or relative to the run day — any "N days" / "N weeks" / "N months" / "N years" or "today" ("1 day" = since yesterday) — so a schedule never needs editing. Empty (default) = no date cut. Use for "only new reviews since last run": with most_recent order the walk stops at the first page older than the cut, so a daily run reads a page or two; older reviews are never billed. No memory between runs: dedupe on review_id.

dateRange.title: Date range
dateRange.description: Trustpilot's own date window, applied on their servers: "all" (default), "last30days", "last3months", "last6months", "last12months". Reviews outside it are never fetched or billed. Use for "reviews from the last 3 months"; sinceDate gives an exact day.

keyword.title: Keyword
keyword.description: Only reviews whose text mentions this word or phrase, e.g. "refund", "delivery", "chargeback" (up to 100 characters). Empty (default) = no keyword filter. This is Trustpilot's own review search, so non-matching reviews are never fetched or billed. It searches review text, not company names: to choose a company use companyDomains.

languages.title: Language
languages.description: "all" (default) = reviews in every language, each row tagged with its language code. One code — "en", "de", "fr", "es", "it", "nl", "da", "sv" — keeps that language only, applied by Trustpilot so other languages are never fetched or billed. Trustpilot's own page shows English only, which hides most reviews of a global brand; the free company row lists how many reviews each language holds. Reviews come back as written, never translated.

verifiedOnly.title: Verified reviews only
verifiedOnly.description: true = only reviews Trustpilot marks verified (invited after a real transaction, or identity-checked); unverified reviews are never fetched or billed. false (default) = every review, with verified and verification_level on each row. Many companies collect few verified reviews, so true can return far fewer rows.

requireText.title: Require review text
requireText.description: true = drop reviews that carry only a star rating and a title, before billing. false (default) = keep them, with text null. Use for sentiment analysis or any text corpus. Applied after the maxReviewsPerCompany cap, so 100 asked may deliver fewer than 100.

includeCompanyRow.title: Include company row
includeCompanyRow.description: true (default) = one free row per company (type "company"): trust_score, stars, review_count, reviews_last_12_months, ratings (the 1-5 star histogram), review_languages, categories, website, country_code, email, phone, address, is_claimed, is_closed, is_collecting, verified_payment, verified_identity, url. Use for "what is company X's TrustScore": there is no summary-only switch, so set maxReviewsPerCompany 1 and the run bills one review per company ($0.0015). false = no company row.
includeCompanyRow.sectionDescription: What lands in the dataset besides the reviews themselves.

deepPaging.title: Go past Trustpilot's 200-review wall
deepPaging.description: true (default) = when more than 200 reviews are asked for, each star rating (1 to 5) is fetched as its own 200-review view, merged and de-duplicated: up to 1000 reviews per company. The merged set is the newest 200 of each star rating, not the 1000 newest overall: for a strictly chronological sample stay at 200 or slice with sinceDate / dateRange. false = one view only, never more than 200 reviews or 10 page requests per company. No effect on the price per review.
deepPaging.sectionDescription: How the actor gets past Trustpilot's 200-review wall for anonymous visitors.

sessions.title: Parallel sessions
sessions.description: Proxy sessions (egress IPs) fetching pages in parallel, 1 to 8, e.g. 2 (default). Each is paced separately; raise it for a long company list.
sessions.sectionDescription: Trustpilot answers every plain request with an AWS WAF challenge. The actor solves it once in a headless browser (5-20 seconds), then fetches every page without a browser on the token that challenge issued, refreshed every four minutes.

perIp.title: Requests per second per session
perIp.description: Requests per second per session, 0.2 to 2, e.g. 1 (default). 1 is what Trustpilot tolerates comfortably; higher values earn retries, not speed.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Apify Proxy, RESIDENTIAL group (the default, and required: the headless browser that solves Trustpilot's AWS WAF challenge runs through it, once per four-minute token window). Leave the default.

description: Trustpilot customer reviews. Minimal input: {"companyDomains": ["www.booking.com"]} (or startUrls with a review-page URL). maxReviewsPerCompany defaults to 100 (up to $0.15 per company at $0.0015 a review): set 1000 for a full corpus, or maxRating 2 + sinceDate "7 days" for a daily complaints feed. Every filter runs before billing.
